_comment: Editable defaults. Numbers marked 'aggregator' are order-of-magnitude, not measured by us. Replace with your own: run llama-bench / ollama run --verbose and read power with `sudo powermetrics --samplers gpu_power` (macOS) or `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=power.draw --format=csv` (NVIDIA). Prices are street prices in USD at review date.
_laptop_note: The MacBook Pro profile is the only laptop here and it behaves differently from the desktops: (a) sustained tok/s drops a few percent below the identically-specced Mac Studio M4 Max once the chassis heat-soaks, because a laptop cooler cannot hold peak clocks for a multi-hour agent session; (b) 48 GB unified memory is the binding constraint, not throughput -- macOS caps GPU-usable memory at roughly 75 % of it by default, so ~36 GB, which fits 32B-class models at Q4 but NOT gpt-oss-120b (~63 GB) or Llama 3.3 70B Q4 (~40 GB). Those models are therefore absent from its tok_s tables on purpose; (c) on battery, macOS reduces sustained GPU power further. All laptop figures are estimates.

macbook-pro-16-m4-max-48gb.label: MacBook Pro 16in M4 Max, 48 GB (laptop)
macbook-pro-16-m4-max-48gb.source: Apple US list price for the 16in M4 Max 48 GB/1 TB build (approx., re-check at apple.com). Power: 140 W adapter; 75 W is an ESTIMATE of sustained *system* draw during LLM decode, which is memory-bandwidth-bound rather than power-bound, so it sits well below the ~110-120 W this chassis pulls under an all-core CPU+GPU burn. A laptop also throttles on prolonged load where a Mac Studio does not -- see the _laptop_note below.
